definition_zh: 回忆起；召回；撤销；记忆力
definition_en: to remember something from the past; to order a person or product back; to cancel officially; the power to remember
core_image: 一只手指向身后，把远处的画面拉回眼前
scene: 老人翻开旧相册，指着一张褪色的照片停住。She could still recall the smell of her grandmother's kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 recall 是「回忆起」（第 1 个义项：把过去的记忆唤回）；句意为她仍能回忆起祖母厨房里的味道。画面里可留意：翻开的相册、褪色的照片。

senses.title: To remember
senses.definition: to bring a past event or detail back into the mind
senses.definitionCN: 把过去的事件或细节重新带回心里
senses.example: She could still recall the smell of her grandmother's kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍能回忆起祖母厨房里的味道。
senses.why: Re- means back, and call means to summon, so the word pictures a memory being called back to the present.
senses.whyCN: re- 意为「回」，call 意为「召唤」，因此这个词描绘记忆被唤回当下。

senses.title: To call back
senses.definition: to order a person or a product to return
senses.definitionCN: 命令某个人或某件产品返回
senses.example: The company recalled thousands of faulty toys.
senses.exampleCN: 公司召回了数千件有缺陷的玩具。
senses.why: The literal image of calling someone back became an official order to return, first for envoys and later for goods.
senses.whyCN: 把某人唤回的字面形象，变成了正式的返回命令，先是针对使节，后来针对商品。

senses.title: To cancel officially
senses.definition: to withdraw a decision, an offer, or a law by official action
senses.definitionCN: 以官方行动撤回决定、提议或法律
senses.example: The council recalled the unpopular rule.
senses.exampleCN: 议会撤销了那条不受欢迎的规定。
senses.why: A cancelled decision is sent back to those who made it, and the image of calling back covers that reversal.
senses.whyCN: 被撤销的决定被送回做出决定的人那里，而「唤回」的形象正涵盖这种反转。

senses.title: The power to remember
senses.definition: the ability to remember things, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 记住事物的能力，作名词使用
senses.example: His recall of names is remarkably quick.
senses.exampleCN: 他记名字的速度快得惊人。
senses.why: When the act of calling back is viewed as a capacity, the verb turns into a noun naming memory itself.
senses.whyCN: 当「唤回」这一行为被视为一种能力时，动词就转为指称记忆本身的名词。

intro.en: Recall is a native calling verb with a Latin prefix: to call back is first a voice, then a memory, then an order.
intro.cn: recall 是本族的「呼喊」动词加拉丁前缀：唤回先是声音，再是记忆，最后是命令。

items.en: Ceallian meant to call out, the native verb behind call.
items.cn: ceallian 意为呼喊，是 call 背后的本族动词。

items.en: Norse kalla, to call, reinforced the same verb in northern English.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kalla（呼喊）在英格兰北部强化了同一个动词。

items.en: The Latin prefix re-, meaning back, joined call to make recall.
items.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 意为「回」，与 call 结合成 recall。

items.en: Middle English recallen meant both to call back and to remember.
items.cn: 中古英语 recallen 既指唤回，也指记起。

items.en: Modern English extended recall to products, officials, and the noun for memory.
items.cn: 现代英语把 recall 扩展到产品、官员，以及表记忆的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs with a similar opening; the near-meaning group gathers words for remembering and for summoning back.
note.cn: 形近组收开头相似的动词；近义组收表记忆与唤回的词。

entries.definition: To keep or bring back in mind.
To gather memories back with effort.

normalIntro.en: The word is call plus back: a voice calls, and what was distant returns.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 call 加「回」：声音一唤，远处的东西就回来。

normal.en: Re plus call: to call back a face, a product, or a rule.
normal.cn: re 加 call：把面孔、产品或规定唤回来。

normal.en: Recall a memory is the everyday sense; product recall is the official one.
normal.cn: recall a memory 是日常义；product recall 是官方义。

normal.en: The noun has the same spelling, so recall can name the power to remember.
normal.cn: 名词拼写相同，因此 recall 也能指记忆力。

normal.en: Beyond recall means so far gone that it cannot be called back.
normal.cn: beyond recall 意为久远到再也唤不回来。

normal.en: Keep the double l: recall, recalled, recalling.
normal.cn: 注意双写 l：recall、recalled、recalling。

abstract.en: Memory is a call across time, and the past answers only if it still lives in us.
abstract.cn: 记忆是穿越时间的一次呼唤，过去只有在仍活在我们心里时才会应答。

abstract.en: A recall of a product is an admission that something once sold should not have been.
abstract.cn: 召回产品，就是承认某件已售出之物本不该售出。

abstract.en: What a society chooses to recall is what it chooses to be.
abstract.cn: 一个社会选择记住什么，就是选择成为什么。

examples.en: She could still recall the smell of her grandmother's kitchen.
examples.cn: 她仍能回忆起祖母厨房里的味道。

examples.en: The company recalled thousands of faulty toys.
examples.cn: 公司召回了数千件有缺陷的玩具。

examples.en: His recall of names is remarkably quick.
examples.cn: 他记名字的速度快得惊人。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 call（呼唤）：把记忆唤回来就是回忆；把人或产品唤回来就是召回。

root: 古英语 ceallian / 古诺斯语 kalla（呼喊）+ 前缀 re-（回）→ 中古英语 recallen → 现代英语 recall；同族有 recalling、recallable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is calling something back; the senses move from memory to products, to cancelled decisions, and to memory as a power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西唤回」；义项从记忆，到产品，到被撤销的决定，最后到作为一种能力的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pointing backwards, pulling a distant scene into view.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指向身后，把远处的画面拉回眼前。

branches.en: a face rising from an old photograph
branches.cn: 一张脸从旧照片里浮起

branches.en: toys pulled from shop shelves
branches.cn: 玩具从货架上被收回

branches.en: a rule struck from the book
branches.cn: 一条规定被从册子上划去

branches.en: a quick list of names in the mind
branches.cn: 脑中飞快列出的一串名字

branches.en: a memory called back and a decision called back
branches.cn: 唤回记忆，也撤回决定

intro.en: A native English verb of calling takes a Latin prefix, and the resulting word spreads from voices to memories and to official orders.
intro.cn: 英语本族的「呼喊」动词接上拉丁前缀，所得之词从声音扩展到记忆与官方命令。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is the prefix re-, meaning back; the verb call is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁元素是前缀 re-，意为「回」；动词 call 是英语本族词。

definition_en: to take into one's hands or possession; to welcome a guest; to pick up a signal; to experience something
core_image: 双手向前摊开，接住递来的东西
scene: 酒店门口，前台人员侧身让客人先进门。The hotel receives guests from all over the world.
sceneCN: 这里 receives 是「接待」（第 2 个义项：迎接客人）；句意为这家酒店接待来自世界各地的客人。画面里可留意：门口侧身让路的前台、摊开的双手。

senses.title: To get what is sent
senses.definition: to take into one's hands or possession something that has been sent or given
senses.definitionCN: 把寄来或给予的东西拿到手中或归于自己
senses.example: She received a letter from her old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她收到了老教师寄来的一封信。
senses.why: Recipere joined re-, back, and capere, to take, so the word pictures taking something that comes to you.
senses.whyCN: recipere 由 re-（回）与 capere（拿取）组成，因此这个词描绘把送到你面前的东西收下。

senses.title: To welcome a guest
senses.definition: to greet and welcome someone who arrives
senses.definitionCN: 迎接并款待到来的人
senses.example: The hotel receives guests from all over the world.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店接待来自世界各地的客人。
senses.why: A guest is also something that comes to you, so the same verb covers taking a person in.
senses.whyCN: 客人也是来到你面前的人，因此同一个动词也涵盖把一个人迎进来。

senses.title: To pick up a signal
senses.definition: to catch and translate a broadcast or electronic signal
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉并转换广播或电子信号
senses.example: The old radio can still receive short-wave signals.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧收音机仍能接收短波信号。
senses.why: A message arriving through the air is taken in by the set, so the same verb covers signals.
senses.whyCN: 通过空气传来的信息被机器收进来，因此同一个动词也用于信号。

senses.title: To experience something
senses.definition: to be given a reaction, a treatment, or an impression
senses.definitionCN: 得到某种反应、对待或印象
senses.example: The plan received strong criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案受到了强烈的批评。
senses.why: To receive a reaction is to have it delivered to you, even when the thing delivered is unpleasant.
senses.whyCN: 受到某种反应，就是让反应落到自己身上，即使落到身上的东西并不愉快。

intro.en: Receive is a Latin taking verb that came through French, and its image of open hands extends to guests, signals, and reactions.
intro.cn: receive 是经法语传来的拉丁「拿取」动词，其「摊开双手」的形象延伸到客人、信号与反应。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, the core of the whole family.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取或抓住，是整个词族的核心。

items.en: Recipere added re-, back, to capere, giving the sense of taking something in.
items.cn: recipere 在 capere 前加 re-（回），得到「把东西收进来」的意思。

items.en: Old French receivre carried the verb into English with its broad sense of taking.
items.cn: 古法语 receivre 把这个动词带入英语，保留了宽泛的「拿取」义。

items.en: Middle English receiven already covered letters, guests, and blows.
items.cn: 中古英语 receiven 已涵盖信件、客人，以及打击。

items.en: Modern English added signals and medical treatment to the older range.
items.cn: 现代英语在旧有范围上又加入了信号与医疗。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words of getting and welcoming.
note.cn: 形近组收相同结尾音的动词；近义组收表获得与迎接的词。

entries.definition: To make someone believe what is false.
To form an idea or a plan.
To get something, often with effort.

normalIntro.en: The word pictures open hands: whatever comes, a letter or a guest, is taken in.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词描绘摊开的双手：无论来的是信还是客人，都被收进来。

normal.en: Re plus ceive: to take back what was sent to you.
normal.cn: re 加 ceive：把寄给你的东西收下来。

normal.en: Received is the past form, so write receive, received, receiving.
normal.cn: 过去式是 received，拼写为 receive、received、receiving。

normal.en: Receive guests is the formal way to say welcome them.
normal.cn: receive guests 是「迎接客人」的正式说法。

normal.en: A radio receives a signal with no hands at all.
normal.cn: 收音机接收信号，完全不用手。

normal.en: Receive criticism uses the same verb as receive a gift.
normal.cn: receive criticism 与 receive a gift 用的是同一个动词。

abstract.en: To receive is to accept that something comes from outside oneself.
abstract.cn: 接收就是承认有些东西来自自身之外。

abstract.en: A receiver must be open; a closed hand receives nothing.
abstract.cn: 接收者必须敞开，握紧的手什么也接不到。

abstract.en: Receiving a reaction is the price of having acted at all.
abstract.cn: 受到反应，是曾经行动过的代价。

examples.en: She received a letter from her old teacher.
examples.cn: 她收到了老教师寄来的一封信。

examples.en: The hotel receives guests from all over the world.
examples.cn: 这家酒店接待来自世界各地的客人。

examples.en: The plan received strong criticism.
examples.cn: 这个方案受到了强烈的批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 ceive（拿取）：把送来的东西拿回来，就是收到；把客人迎进来，就是接待。

root: 拉丁 recipere（re- 回 + capere 拿取）→ 古法语 receivre → 中古英语 receiven → 英语 receive；同族有 receiver、reception、receipt。

sensesIntro.en: The core is taking something in; the senses move from things to guests, to signals, and to reactions.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西收进来」；义项从物品，到客人，到信号，再到反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two open hands catching what is handed over.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只摊开的手接住递来的东西。

branches.en: a letter placed in the palm
branches.cn: 一封信落在掌心

branches.en: a guest stepping inside
branches.cn: 客人迈步进门

branches.en: an aerial picking up a wave
branches.cn: 天线捕捉到一道波

branches.en: a harsh remark landing
branches.cn: 一句严厉的话落到身上

branches.en: a thing received and a person welcomed
branches.cn: 收下物品，也迎进客人

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin verb for taking, with prefixes and English suffixes adding direction and agents.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语的「拿取」动词上，前缀与英语后缀补充方向与施动者。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is capere, to take, with re- meaning back; French carried it to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁核心是 capere（拿取），前缀 re- 意为「回」；法语把它带到英语。

items.meaning: one who or that which receives

definition_en: happening or existing a short time ago; fresh and up to date; belonging to modern times
core_image: 日历上刚翻过的一页，墨迹还新
scene: 报纸头版印着前一天发生的事，纸边还带着油墨味。Recent research suggests that sleep affects memory.
sceneCN: 这里 recent 是「最近的」（第 1 个义项：不久前发生的）；句意为近期研究表明睡眠会影响记忆。画面里可留意：刚翻过的日历、带油墨味的报纸。

senses.title: Happening a short time ago
senses.definition: happening or existing only a short time before the present
senses.definitionCN: 在当下之前不久发生或存在的
senses.example: Recent research suggests that sleep affects memory.
senses.exampleCN: 近期研究表明睡眠会影响记忆。
senses.why: Latin recens meant fresh or just made, and English kept the sense of something still close in time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 recens 意为新鲜的、刚做成的，英语保留了「在时间上仍然靠近」的含义。

senses.title: Fresh and up to date
senses.definition: containing the newest information and not yet replaced
senses.definitionCN: 包含最新信息、尚未被取代的
senses.example: The library keeps recent issues of the journal.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆保留了这份期刊最新的几期。
senses.why: What is fresh is also current, so the word came to describe information that has not been overtaken.
senses.whyCN: 新鲜的东西也是当下的，于是这个词用来形容尚未被超越的信息。

senses.title: Belonging to modern times
senses.definition: of a period close to the present, especially in history or geology
senses.definitionCN: 属于靠近当下的时期，尤其用于历史或地质分期
senses.example: Recent history covers the last two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 近代史涵盖过去两个世纪。
senses.why: From a few days ago the word widened to a whole historical period that is close to the present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「几天前」扩展到整个靠近当下的历史时期。

intro.en: Recent comes straight from a Latin adjective of freshness, and its sense widened from fresh things to fresh time and fresh periods.
intro.cn: recent 直接来自拉丁语表「新鲜」的形容词，其含义从新鲜之物扩展到新鲜的时间与时期。

items.en: Recens meant fresh, new, or just made, said of things still new to the senses.
items.cn: recens 意为新鲜的、新的、刚做成的，用于感官上仍新的事物。

items.en: The comparative recentior meant more recent, the form behind the English degree forms.
items.cn: 比较级 recentior 意为「更近期的」，是英语比较形式的来源。

items.en: Old French recent brought the adjective into English unchanged in sense.
items.cn: 古法语 recent 把这个形容词原样带入英语，含义未变。

items.en: Middle English recent applied the word to events and to writing.
items.cn: 中古英语 recent 把这个词用于事件与文字。

items.en: Modern English extended recent to news, research, and whole historical periods.
items.cn: 现代英语把 recent 扩展到新闻、研究以及整个历史时期。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adjectives close in sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for newness and currency.
note.cn: 形近组收读音相近的形容词；近义组收表新鲜与当下的词。

entries.definition: One who rules in another's place.
The most recent of a series.
Of the present or near past.

normalIntro.en: The word pictures something still warm from happening, like a page just turned.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词描绘刚刚发生、还带着热度的事物，像刚翻过的一页日历。

normal.en: Recent sounds like re-sent, as if news was just sent to you.
normal.cn: recent 听起来像 re-sent，仿佛消息刚刚发给你。

normal.en: In recent years is the standard phrase for the near past.
normal.cn: in recent years 是表达「近年来」的标准搭配。

normal.en: Recent research means work published not long ago.
normal.cn: recent research 指不久前发表的研究。

normal.en: The comparison uses more recent, not recenter.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more recent，而不是 recenter。

normal.en: Recent history is a period; a recent event is a moment.
normal.cn: recent history 是一段时期，a recent event 是一个瞬间。

abstract.en: The recent is the edge of time, where memory has not yet become history.
abstract.cn: 「最近的」是时间的边缘，记忆尚未变成历史。

abstract.en: What is recent feels important precisely because it is still warm.
abstract.cn: 刚发生的事显得重要，正因为它还带着温度。

abstract.en: Every age calls its own news recent and the rest old.
abstract.cn: 每个时代都把自己的新闻称为「最近的」，把其余称为旧的。

examples.en: Recent research suggests that sleep affects memory.
examples.cn: 近期研究表明睡眠会影响记忆。

examples.en: The library keeps recent issues of the journal.
examples.cn: 图书馆保留了这份期刊最新的几期。

examples.en: Recent history covers the last two centuries.
examples.cn: 近代史涵盖过去两个世纪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 recent 联想成「日历刚翻过去的一页」：墨迹还新，就是最近的。

root: 拉丁 recens（新鲜的、刚出现的）→ 古法语 recent → 中古英语 recent → 英语 recent；同族有 recently、recency、recentness。

sensesIntro.en: The core is freshness in time; the senses move from a recent event to current information and to a modern period.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「时间上的新鲜」；义项从刚发生的事，到当下的信息，再到近代时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar page just turned, the ink still fresh.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历刚翻过的一页，墨迹还新。

branches.en: a newspaper from yesterday
branches.cn: 昨天的报纸

branches.en: a journal issue on the shelf
branches.cn: 架子上最新一期期刊

branches.en: a chapter on the last two centuries
branches.cn: 讲述过去两个世纪的一章

branches.en: a recent event and recent data
branches.cn: 刚发生的事与最新的数据

branches.en: fresh news and modern history
branches.cn: 新鲜的新闻与近代的历史

intro.en: A short Latin adjective of freshness gives the base, and English endings produce the adverb and the nouns.
intro.cn: 一个表新鲜的简短拉丁形容词提供词根，英语词尾则造出副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is recens, with the comparative recentior behind the English degree forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 recens，其比较级 recentior 是英语比较形式的来源。

definition_en: not long ago; during the period just before now; newly
core_image: 手机屏上一条刚收到的消息，时间标着「刚刚」
scene: 会议室的同事指着屏幕上刚发布的公告，语速很快。She recently joined the research team.
sceneCN: 这里 recently 是「最近」（第 1 个义项：不久前）；句意为她最近加入了研究团队。画面里可留意：刚收到的消息、屏幕上的公告。

senses.title: Not long ago
senses.definition: at a point in the near past, not long before now
senses.definitionCN: 在不久前的某个时点
senses.example: She recently joined the research team.
senses.exampleCN: 她最近加入了研究团队。
senses.why: The adjective recent means fresh in time, and -ly turns it into the adverb of a near past moment.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 recent 意为时间上新鲜的，加上 -ly 就成为表「不久前某一时点」的副词。

senses.title: Lately
senses.definition: during the period just before the present, seen as a stretch of time
senses.definitionCN: 在当下之前的一段时期里
senses.example: The weather has been unusually warm recently.
senses.exampleCN: 近来天气异常暖和。
senses.why: The same adverb covers a single moment and a stretch, because a recent period is made of recent moments.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词既覆盖单个时点，也覆盖一段时期，因为「近期」正是由一个个「最近」组成。

senses.title: Newly in a role
senses.definition: at a time only shortly before now, especially after a change of status
senses.definitionCN: 在不久前，尤指身份刚发生改变之后
senses.example: The recently elected mayor promised reform.
senses.exampleCN: 新近当选的市长承诺推行改革。
senses.why: A change that has just happened leaves a person newly in a state, and the adverb marks that freshness of status.
senses.whyCN: 刚刚发生的变化让人处于一种新状态，这个副词正是标记身份的新鲜。

intro.en: Recently is the Latin adjective of freshness plus the English suffix of manner; a fresh moment becomes a fresh stretch of time.
intro.cn: recently 是拉丁语表新鲜的形容词加英语表方式的后缀；新鲜的瞬间由此变为新鲜的一段时间。

items.en: Recens meant fresh or just made, said of things still new.
items.cn: recens 意为新鲜的、刚做成的，用于仍然新的事物。

items.en: Old French recent carried the adjective into English without changing its sense.
items.cn: 古法语 recent 把这个形容词原样带入英语。

items.en: The native suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb of time and manner.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -ly 把形容词变为表时间与方式的副词。

items.en: Modern English uses recently for a near past moment and for the period just passed.
items.cn: 现代英语用 recently 指不久的过去时点，也指刚过去的一段时期。

items.en: The adverb widened from one moment to a whole stretch of recent time.
items.cn: 这个副词从单个瞬间扩展到整段近期时间。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective base and two words close in sound; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of the near past.
note.cn: 形近组收形容词原形与两个音近词；近义组收表「不久前」的副词。

entries.definition: In a proper and acceptable way.
In the time just before now.
Just now, in a fresh state.

normalIntro.en: The word is recent plus ly: what is fresh in time becomes an adverb of the near past.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 recent 加 ly：时间上新鲜的东西，变成表「不久前」的副词。

normal.en: Recent plus -ly: in a recent way, or in recent time.
normal.cn: recent 加 -ly：以最近的方式，或在最近的时间里。

normal.en: Until recently means up to a point not long ago.
normal.cn: until recently 意为直到不久前。

normal.en: Recently arrived describes a person or thing that has just come.
normal.cn: recently arrived 形容刚到的人或物。

normal.en: The comparison is more recently, never recentlier.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more recently，绝不是 recentlier。

normal.en: Keep the t before ly: recently, not recenly.
normal.cn: ly 前要保留 t：recently，而不是 recenly。

abstract.en: Recently is where memory and news overlap, still warm enough to matter.
abstract.cn: 「最近」是记忆与新闻重叠的地方，还热得足以重要。

abstract.en: A thing done recently can still be undone; that is its power.
abstract.cn: 最近做成的事仍可被撤回，这就是它的力量。

abstract.en: We call the near past recent because we have not finished living it.
abstract.cn: 我们称近过去为「最近」，因为我们还没把它过完。

examples.en: She recently joined the research team.
examples.cn: 她最近加入了研究团队。

examples.en: The weather has been unusually warm recently.
examples.cn: 近来天气异常暖和。

examples.en: The recently elected mayor promised reform.
examples.cn: 新近当选的市长承诺推行改革。

dict_mnemonic.text: recent（最近的）加 ly（地）：最近的时点、近来的一段日子，都是 recently。

root: 拉丁 recens（新鲜的）→ 英语 recent + 后缀 -ly → recently；同族有 recency、recentness。

sensesIntro.en: The core is temporal freshness; the senses move from one near moment to a recent stretch and to a newly changed status.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「时间上的新鲜」；义项从一个临近的时点，到一段近期，再到刚改变的身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a message on a screen stamped just now.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上一条刚收到的消息，时间标着「刚刚」。

branches.en: a screen stamped just now
branches.cn: 屏幕上刚打上的时间

branches.en: a warm week in a cold month
branches.cn: 寒冷月份里暖和的一周

branches.en: a newly elected mayor
branches.cn: 新近当选的市长

branches.en: a moment and a stretch of time
branches.cn: 一个瞬间与一段时间

branches.en: lately and newly
branches.cn: 近来与新近

intro.en: A Latin adjective of freshness takes two English suffixes, one for state and one for manner, to become an adverb of time.
intro.cn: 表新鲜的拉丁形容词接上两个英语后缀，一个表状态，一个表方式，成为表时间的副词。

latinIntro.en: The base recens is Latin, and the comparative recentior explains the English degree forms.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 recens 是拉丁语，其比较级 recentior 解释了英语的比较形式。

definition_zh: 食谱；烹饪法；配方；秘诀；方法
definition_en: a set of instructions for preparing a dish, or a method for achieving something
core_image: 一张写满步骤的卡片：照着做就能端出一盘好菜
scene: 厨房里，奶奶从铁盒里抽出一张泛黄的卡片递给孙女。Grandma handed me her secret recipe for apple pie.
sceneCN: 这里 recipe 是「食谱、配方」（第 1 个义项：做菜的步骤说明）；句意为奶奶把她做苹果派的秘方交给了我。画面里可留意：泛黄的卡片、铁盒、递过去的手。

collocations.zh: 招致灾难的做法；后患无穷

derivatives.zh: 由 re-（回来）+ cite 词根派生的同族词，义为「独奏会；朗诵」（词义已偏移到表演领域）
同根 recipere 加名词化，义为「收据；接收」（与 recipe 词义已分道）

senses.title: Instructions for cooking a dish
senses.definition: a written set of instructions telling you how to prepare and cook a particular food
senses.definitionCN: 写明如何准备和烹制某种食物的一组步骤说明
senses.example: This soup needs two eggs according to the recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 按食谱，这道汤需要放两个鸡蛋。
senses.why: The Latin root recipere means to take or receive; a recipe was originally a medical prescription, a list of things the cook or apothecary was to take.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 recipere 意为「取、拿」，recipe 最早是药方——一张列明「要取哪些材料」的单子，后来从药房转进厨房，变成照单取料做菜的步骤单。

senses.title: A formula or mixture in medicine or industry
senses.definition: a set of ingredients and proportions used to make something, especially in medicine or manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 用于制药或制造某物的成分及比例组合
senses.example: The company keeps the formula as a carefully guarded recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把这款配方当作严守的商业机密。
senses.why: Since recipes began as prescriptions written by physicians, the sense of a precise mixture of ingredients stayed in technical fields even after the cooking sense took over.
senses.whyCN: recipe 本义就是医师写下的处方， specifying 成分与比例；烹饪义普及后，这个「精确配方」义仍留在医药和工业领域，成为第二条义项。

senses.title: A method for achieving a result
senses.titleCN: 秘诀；方法（常喻好坏结果）
senses.definition: a way of doing something that will produce a particular result, often used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 能产生某种结果的做法，多用于比喻，常指带来坏结果
senses.example: Cutting sleep to five hours is a recipe for exhaustion.
senses.exampleCN: 把睡眠压缩到五个小时，只会换来疲惫不堪。
senses.why: A formula reliably produces its product; by metaphor, any reliable combination of actions 'produces' an outcome, whether good or bad.
senses.whyCN: 配方按固定比例就能稳定产出成品；比喻开来，一套固定的行事组合也会稳定「产出」某种结局，所以引申出「注定导致……的做法」。

intro.en: Recipe comes from Latin recipere, and it began life not in the kitchen but in the pharmacy.
intro.cn: recipe 源自拉丁语 recipere（取、拿），它的出生地不是厨房，而是药房。

items.en: recipere, from re- (back) + capere (to take), meant 'to take back, receive'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 recipere 由 re-（回）+ capere（拿）构成，意为「取回、接收」。

items.en: In medical manuscripts, recipes began with the imperative 'Recipe!' — 'Take (the following ingredients)'.
items.cn: 在中世纪医学手稿里，药方以命令式 Recipe! 开头，意为「取下列药材」。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as a term on physicians' prescriptions.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语，仍指医师处方上的用语。

items.en: English took over the word in the 14th century, first for medical prescriptions.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入该词，最初仍指药方、处方。

items.en: By the 17th to 18th centuries the cooking sense dominated, and later the figurative sense 'a recipe for disaster' appeared.
items.cn: 十七到十八世纪起烹饪义占主流，后来又出现「招致灾难的做法」这类比喻用法。

note.en: These words are often confused with recipe because of spelling or meaning.
note.cn: 下列词与 recipe 或形近易混，或义场相邻。

entries.definition: a paper proving you paid for something; the act of receiving
entries.definitionCN: 收据；接收（与 recipe 拼写极近，词源同族但词义不同）

entries.definition: to say aloud a poem or list from memory
entries.definitionCN: 背诵；朗诵（只是拼写相近，词源为 citare「唤起」，并非同源）
接受者；受领者（同出 recipere 词族）

entries.definition: a fixed form of words or a set of ingredients for a result
entries.definitionCN: 公式；配方（偏技术、固定化）

entries.definition: a doctor's written order for medicine
entries.definitionCN: 处方（recipe 的现代医学对应词）

entries.definition: a planned way of doing something
entries.definitionCN: 方法；办法（泛指做法，不限材料配比）

normalIntro.en: Root-based reminders for recipe.
normalIntro.cn: recipe 的词根式记忆提示。

normal.en: re- (back) + cip (take) + e: what you 'take' to make the dish.
normal.cn: re-（回）+ cip（拿）+ e：照单「取」来下锅的，就是食谱。

normal.en: Same root family as receive, receipt, recipient.
normal.cn: 与 receive、receipt、recipient 同属「拿取」词族。

normal.en: Medieval prescriptions began with 'Recipe!' meaning 'take these'.
normal.cn: 中世纪药方开头就是 Recipe!（取药），可见词的本义。

normal.en: Collocation anchor: a recipe for disaster = a formula producing disaster.
normal.cn: 搭配锚点：a recipe for disaster，即「产出灾难的配方」。

normal.en: Compare receipt: both from recipere, but one proves payment.
normal.cn: 对照 receipt：同根不同义，receipt 是付款凭证。

abstract.en: Picture a yellowed card in grandma's tin box, steps written in ink.
abstract.cn: 想象奶奶铁盒里那张泛黄的卡片，墨水写着一步步的做法。

abstract.en: Imagine a pharmacist shouting 'Take!' at shelves of herbs.
abstract.cn: 想象药剂师对着药草架喊一声「取！」，那是 recipe 的起点。

abstract.en: See ingredients pouring into one pot in fixed ratios.
abstract.cn: 看见材料按固定比例倒进同一口锅——配方即比例。

examples.en: Follow the recipe step by step and the bread will rise.
examples.cn: 照着食谱一步步做，面包就能发起来。

examples.en: Her secret recipe has been passed down for four generations.
examples.cn: 她的秘方已经传了四代人。

examples.en: Ignoring the weather forecast is a recipe for disaster on a mountain trip.
examples.cn: 登山不看天气预报，注定要出乱子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞塞皮」——「瑞士塞来的皮」配方要照单取料；联想成一张塞到手里的配方卡，记 recipe 是「食谱、配方」。

root: 拉丁语 recipere（取、拿）：re-（回）+ capere（拿）。recipe 原为处方用语 Recipe!（取下列药材），后转为食谱与配方义；同根词 receive、receipt、recipient。

sensesIntro.en: From pharmacy to kitchen to figurative speech: recipe keeps its core image of 'take exactly what is listed'.
sensesIntro.cn: 从药房到厨房再到比喻：recipe 的核心意象始终是「照单取料」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: take exactly what the list says
core.cn: 核心意象：照单取料，按固定清单行事

branches.en: Cooking instructions built from a list of ingredients.
branches.cn: 以材料清单为基础的烹饪步骤（义项 01）。

branches.en: A precise mixture in medicine or industry.
branches.cn: 医药或工业领域的精确配方（义项 02）。

branches.en: A formula reliably yields its product.
branches.cn: 配方按固定比例稳定产出（义项 02、03）。

branches.en: Figurative: a way of doing things predicts the outcome.
branches.cn: 比喻义：固定做法预示结局（义项 03）。

branches.en: Recipes and disaster formulas both promise a result.
branches.cn: 食谱与「灾难配方」都承诺一个结果（义项 01、03）。

intro.en: Recipe carries the Latin take-structure re- + cap.
intro.cn: recipe 携带拉丁语「取拿」结构 re- + cap。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives from capere (to take).
latinIntro.cn: 来自 capere（拿取）的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a list of what to take

definition_zh: 记录；最高纪录；唱片；录制；档案
definition_en: a written or stored account; the best result achieved; a disc of music; to set down or capture for later use
core_image: 厚厚的登记簿上，一行行墨迹整齐排列
scene: 田径场上计时牌停在新的世界最好成绩，看台上掌声四起。She broke the world record in the final race.
sceneCN: 这里 record 是「最高纪录」（第 2 个义项：已达成的最好成绩）；句意为她在决赛中打破了世界纪录。画面里可留意：停住的计时牌、看台上的掌声。

pos.zh: 记录；最高纪录；唱片；档案

senses.title: A stored account
senses.definition: a written or stored account of facts, events, or data
senses.definitionCN: 对事实、事件或数据的书面或电子留存
senses.example: The school keeps a record of every student.
senses.exampleCN: 学校保存着每名学生的记录。
senses.why: Recordari meant to bring something back to the heart, that is, to remember, and a record is memory made durable.
senses.whyCN: recordari 意为把某事重新放回心里，也就是记住，而记录就是被固定下来的记忆。

senses.title: The best result achieved
senses.definition: the best performance or result ever reached in a sport or activity
senses.definitionCN: 某项运动或活动中曾达到的最好成绩
senses.example: She broke the world record in the final race.
senses.exampleCN: 她在决赛中打破了世界纪录。
senses.why: A record once meant the line that holds the best result, and the word came to name the best result itself.
senses.whyCN: record 原指记载最好成绩的那一行，后来直接指最好成绩本身。

senses.title: A disc of music
senses.definition: a flat disc on which music or sound is stored
senses.definitionCN: 储存音乐或声音的扁平圆盘
senses.example: He still owns an old jazz record.
senses.exampleCN: 他还留着一张老爵士唱片。
senses.why: Music cut into a disc is a record in the physical sense, because the grooves store the sound.
senses.whyCN: 刻进圆盘的音乐是物理意义上的记录，因为沟槽储存着声音。

senses.title: To capture for later use
senses.definition: to store sound, images, or data so that they can be used later
senses.definitionCN: 把声音、图像或数据储存起来供以后使用
senses.example: They recorded the concert for the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为档案馆录制了这场音乐会。
senses.why: To record is to set something down for later recall, and a machine now performs that setting down.
senses.whyCN: 录制就是把某物记下以备日后回想，如今由机器来完成这一「记下」。

senses.title: An official file
senses.definition: the body of written evidence kept by a court, an office, or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 由法院、机关或机构保存的书面证据集合
senses.example: The court record shows two earlier warnings.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭档案显示此前有两次警告。
senses.why: An official file is a record kept by an institution, and the word widened from a single note to a body of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 官方档案是机构保存的记录，这个词从单条笔记扩展为一整套证据。

intro.en: Record begins at the heart: to remember is to bring a thing back to the heart, and to record is to fix that memory outside the body.
intro.cn: record 始于「心」：记住就是把事物放回心里，而记录则是把这份记忆固定在身体之外。

items.en: Cor, cordis meant heart, the seat of memory in older thought.
items.cn: cor、cordis 意为心，在更早的观念里是记忆所在之处。

items.en: Recordari meant to remember, literally to bring back to the heart.
items.cn: recordari 意为记住，字面就是「重新带回心里」。

items.en: Old French recorder carried both remembering and setting down in writing.
items.cn: 古法语 recorder 同时带有「记住」与「写下」的意思。

items.en: Middle English record named a witness, a written note, and the act of noting.
items.cn: 中古英语 record 指证人、书面笔录，以及记录的行为。

items.en: Modern English added the disc, the machine recording, and the sports best.
items.cn: 现代英语又加入了唱片、机器录制与运动最高成绩。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same cord- core; the near-meaning group gathers words for stored information and discs.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带 cord- 核心的词；近义组收表储存信息与唱片的词。

entries.definition: To tell a story in detail.
A regular written record of events.
A flat round object that stores sound.

normalIntro.en: The word is about memory kept outside the mind: a note, a disc, a file, a best score.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词讲的是存放在头脑之外的记忆：笔记、唱片、档案、最好成绩。

normal.en: Re plus cord: bring it back to the heart, and you remember; write it down, and you record.
normal.cn: re 加 cord：带回心里是记住，写下来就是记录。

normal.en: The noun stress is on the first syllable, the verb stress on the second.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Break a record means to do better than anyone before.
normal.cn: break a record 意为超过此前所有人。

normal.en: On record means officially written down and known.
normal.cn: on record 意为有正式记载。

normal.en: Record a song and keep a record use the same word in two directions.
normal.cn: record a song 与 keep a record 是同一个词的两种方向。

abstract.en: A record is a promise made to the future that this moment happened.
abstract.cn: 记录是对未来作出的承诺：这一刻确实发生过。

abstract.en: What a culture records is what it intends to remember.
abstract.cn: 一个文化记录什么，就是它打算记住什么。

abstract.en: Every record will fall; the keeping of it is what lasts longer.
abstract.cn: 每一项纪录都会被打败，而记录它的行为持续得更久。

examples.en: The school keeps a record of every student.
examples.cn: 学校保存着每名学生的记录。

examples.en: She broke the world record in the final race.
examples.cn: 她在决赛中打破了世界纪录。

examples.en: They recorded the concert for the archive.
examples.cn: 他们为档案馆录制了这场音乐会。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 cord（心）：把事重新放回心里，就是记住；写下来留存，就是记录。

root: 拉丁 cor / cord-（心）→ recordari（回想，把事放回心里）→ 古法语 recorder → 中古英语 record → 英语 record；同族有 recorder、recording。

sensesIntro.en: The core is memory fixed outside the mind; the senses move from a written account to a best result, a disc, an act of capture, and an official file.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「固定在头脑之外的记忆」；义项从书面记录，到最好成绩、唱片、录制行为，再到官方档案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick ledger filled with even lines of ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本厚厚的登记簿，一行行墨迹排列整齐。

branches.en: a ledger open on a desk
branches.cn: 桌上摊开的登记簿

branches.en: a scoreboard frozen at a new best
branches.cn: 停在最好成绩的计分牌

branches.en: a disc spinning on a turntable
branches.cn: 唱机上旋转的唱片

branches.en: a microphone capturing a concert
branches.cn: 捕捉音乐会的麦克风

branches.en: a file drawer marked official
branches.cn: 标着「官方」的档案抽屉

intro.en: The word joins the Latin word for heart to a prefix of return, and then spreads to discs, machines, and files.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语的「心」与表回返的前缀结合，再扩展到唱片、机器与档案。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin base is cor, heart, and recordari, to remember; the prefix re- carries the sense of return.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 cor（心）与 recordari（记住）；前缀 re- 带有「回返」之义。

definition_en: the colour of blood; a red wine; a state of financial loss
core_image: 一面红旗在灰白的街道上格外显眼
scene: 灰白的街道尽头，一面红旗被风吹得鼓起来。She wore a red coat and walked quickly through the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 red 是「红色」（第 1 个义项：血一样的颜色）；句意为她穿着红色外套，快步穿过人群。画面里可留意：被风吹鼓的红旗、人群中的红色外套。

senses.title: The colour of blood
senses.definition: the colour seen in blood, fire, and ripe fruit
senses.definitionCN: 血液、火焰与成熟果实所呈现的颜色
senses.example: She wore a red coat and walked quickly through the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着红色外套，快步穿过人群。
senses.why: Old English read named the colour directly, and the word has stayed basic and concrete ever since.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 rēad 直接命名这种颜色，这个词从此一直是最基础、最具体的词。

senses.title: A red wine
senses.definition: a wine made from dark grapes and served as a drink
senses.definitionCN: 用深色葡萄酿成、作为饮品供应的酒
senses.example: He ordered a glass of red to go with the meat.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯红葡萄酒配肉。
senses.why: The colour of the wine became a short name for the drink, so a glass of red is a glass of red wine.
senses.whyCN: 酒的颜色成了这种饮品的简称，因此 a glass of red 就是一杯红葡萄酒。

senses.title: A state of loss
senses.definition: the condition of spending more than one earns, shown in red ink in accounts
senses.definitionCN: 支出超过收入的状态，账目上以红字表示
senses.example: The company has been in the red for three quarters.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司已经连续三个季度亏损。
senses.why: Accountants once wrote losses in red ink, so being in the red came to mean losing money.
senses.whyCN: 会计曾用红墨水记录亏损，因此 in the red 逐渐表示亏钱。

intro.en: Red is one of the oldest colour words in English, inherited rather than borrowed, and its later senses grew from things that are red.
intro.cn: red 是英语中最古老的颜色词之一，属继承而来而非借用，后来的义项都从「红的事物」生长出来。

items.en: Read was the Old English adjective for the colour of blood.
items.cn: rēad 是古英语中表血色的形容词。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family with Dutch rood and German rot.
items.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语族，同族有荷兰语 rood 与德语 rot。

items.en: All these forms go back to an ancient root meaning red or ruddy.
items.cn: 这些形式都可追溯到意为「红、赤」的古老词根。

items.en: Middle English red simplified the spelling and kept the colour sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 red 简化了拼写，保留了颜色义。

items.en: Modern English extended red to wine, to loss, and to warning signals.
items.cn: 现代英语把 red 扩展到葡萄酒、亏损与警示信号。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that differ by one letter; the near-meaning group gathers shades of red.
note.cn: 形近组收只差一个字母的短词；近义组收各种红色调。

entries.definition: A tall grass growing by water.
A bright red with a hint of orange.
A rich red like the gem.

normalIntro.en: The word is basic and concrete; its later meanings come from red ink, red wine, and red flags.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词基础而具体；后来的含义都来自红墨水、红葡萄酒与红旗。

normal.en: Red is the colour of blood, fire, and ripe fruit.
normal.cn: red 是血、火与成熟果实的颜色。

normal.en: In the red means losing money, because losses were written in red ink.
normal.cn: in the red 意为亏损，因为亏损曾用红墨水记录。

normal.en: A glass of red is a short way to say a glass of red wine.
normal.cn: a glass of red 是「一杯红葡萄酒」的简称。

normal.en: A red flag warns of danger, on a road or in a report.
normal.cn: red flag 在道路或报告中都表示危险信号。

normal.en: The comparison doubles the d: redder, reddest.
normal.cn: 比较级双写 d：redder、reddest。

abstract.en: Red is the colour that demands to be seen before anything else.
abstract.cn: 红色是要求被最先看见的颜色。

abstract.en: Every language gives red to both love and danger.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都把红色同时给了爱与危险。

abstract.en: A number in red is a fact a business cannot ignore.
abstract.cn: 红色的数字，是生意无法忽视的事实。

examples.en: She wore a red coat and walked quickly through the crowd.
examples.cn: 她穿着红色外套，快步穿过人群。

examples.en: He ordered a glass of red to go with the meat.
examples.cn: 他点了一杯红葡萄酒配肉。

examples.en: The company has been in the red for three quarters.
examples.cn: 这家公司已经连续三个季度亏损。

dict_mnemonic.text: red 联想「一面红旗」：最醒目的颜色；账目上的亏损也用红笔记，于是有了 in the red（赤字）。

root: 古英语 rēad（红）→ 中古英语 red → 现代英语 red；同族有 redden、reddish、redness。与拉丁 ruber 同源，但不是借自拉丁语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the colour of blood; the senses move from the colour to red wine and to red ink in accounts.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「血的颜色」；义项从颜色，到红葡萄酒，再到账目上的红字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red flag standing out against a grey street.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰白街道上一面格外显眼的红旗。

chain: A RED FIGURE IN A LEDGER

branches.en: a flag snapping in the wind
branches.cn: 风中猎猎作响的旗

branches.en: a glass of dark wine
branches.cn: 一杯深色的酒

branches.en: a ledger line in red ink
branches.cn: 账本上用红墨水写的一行

branches.en: a colour worn and a colour drunk
branches.cn: 穿在身上的颜色与喝下肚的颜色

branches.en: wine and loss both coded red
branches.cn: 酒与亏损都用红色标记

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its small family is built with English endings for becoming, resembling, and being.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其小词族由表「变成」「相似」与「状态」的英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded; Latin ruber is a cognate from the same ancient root, not a borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁语来源；拉丁语 ruber 是同源的亲属词，并非借用。

definition_en: to throw back light, heat, or sound; to show or express something; to think carefully about
core_image: 静止的湖面把整排山影倒映出来
scene: 清晨湖面没有一丝风，对岸的山被完整地映在水里。The still water reflected the whole line of hills.
sceneCN: 这里 reflected 是 reflect 的过去式，取「反射、映出」（第 1 个义项：把光或影像折回）；句意为静止的水面映出了整排山峦。画面里可留意：没有波纹的湖面、水中的山影。

senses.title: To throw back
senses.definition: to send back light, heat, or sound from a surface
senses.definitionCN: 从表面把光、热或声音送回去
senses.example: The still water reflected the whole line of hills.
senses.exampleCN: 静止的水面映出了整排山峦。
senses.why: The Latin verb is to bend back: a ray meets a surface and is bent away from it, as if the surface refused to keep it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「弯回去」：光线碰到表面后被折开，仿佛表面不肯留下它。

senses.title: To show or stand for
senses.definition: to show the nature or state of something
senses.definitionCN: 显示出某事物的性质或状况
senses.example: The report reflects the concerns of the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告反映了整个村子的关切。
senses.why: A surface that shows an image is a natural picture of a society that shows its own condition in its records.
senses.whyCN: 能映出影像的表面，自然成了「社会借记录显现自身状况」这一用法的比喻。

senses.title: To think carefully
senses.definition: to turn the mind back on an idea or an experience
senses.definitionCN: 把心思转回到某个想法或经历上
senses.example: She sat by the window and reflected on what he had said.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在窗边，思考他刚才说的话。
senses.why: Thinking is a bending back of attention: the mind leaves the outer scene and returns to what it already holds.
senses.whyCN: 思考是注意力的折返：心思离开外在景象，回到自己已经拥有的东西上。

intro.en: Reflect is to bend back; the word begins with light and ends with thought, and the path between them is a single metaphor.
intro.cn: reflect 意为「弯回去」；这个词从光开始，到思想结束，而两者之间的路径只是一个比喻。

items.en: Flectere meant to bend or curve, the base of a family of words about turning.
items.cn: flectere 意为弯曲，是表示「转向」的词族的词根。

items.en: Reflectere joined re-, back, with flectere and meant to bend or turn back.
items.cn: reflectere 由 re-（往回）与 flectere 组成，意为弯回去或转回去。

items.en: Natural philosophers used the word first for rays of light bent back from a surface.
items.cn: 自然哲学家最先用这个词指从表面折回的光线。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the same word described an image in a mirror and a mind turned back on itself.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，同一个词既指镜中的影像，也指回转自身的头脑。

items.en: The sense of showing a condition grew from the mirror: a record reflects what produced it.
items.cn: 「显现状况」这一义从镜子发展而来：一份记录会映出产生它的那个东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the Latin flectere; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of showing, mirroring, and thinking.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁 flectere 构成的动词；近义组收表示映现与思考的动词。

entries.definition: To change the pitch or form of a word.

normalIntro.en: The word is a bending back, whether of light from water or of attention from the world to the self.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「弯回去」，既可以是水面对光的折返，也可以是注意力从外界折回自身。

normal.en: Re plus flectere, back plus bend: light bends back from the water.
normal.cn: re 加 flectere，往回加弯：光从水面弯回来。

normal.en: A mirror reflects your face; a report reflects the facts.
normal.cn: 镜子映出你的脸，报告映出事实。

normal.en: Reflect on a question means to bend your mind back to it.
normal.cn: reflect on a question 指把心思折回到这个问题上。

normal.en: Reflective people think; reflective surfaces shine.
normal.cn: reflective 的人爱思考，reflective 的表面会反光。

normal.en: Do not confuse reflect with deflect, which turns things aside.
normal.cn: 别把 reflect 与 deflect 弄混，后者是把东西拨到一边。

abstract.en: To reflect is to let what is outside pass through you and come back changed.
abstract.cn: 反射，就是让外界之物穿过你，再以改变过的样子回来。

abstract.en: A society is known by what it chooses to reflect on.
abstract.cn: 一个社会因它选择反思什么而为人所知。

abstract.en: The mirror and the mind use the same verb because both return an image.
abstract.cn: 镜子与头脑共用同一个动词，因为两者都送回一个影像。

examples.en: The still water reflected the whole line of hills.
examples.cn: 静止的水面映出了整排山峦。

examples.en: The report reflects the concerns of the whole village.
examples.cn: 这份报告反映了整个村子的关切。

examples.en: She sat by the window and reflected on what he had said.
examples.cn: 她坐在窗边，思考他刚才说的话。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 flect（弯）：光弯回来是反射，事实弯回来是反映，心思弯回来是思考。

root: 拉丁 flectere（弯曲）→ reflectere（弯回去）→ 英语 reflect；同族有 reflection、reflective、reflector，形近的 deflect、inflect、reflex 共用 flectere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bending back; the senses move from a ray returned by a surface, to a record showing its source, to a mind turned back on itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「弯回去」；义项从表面送回的光线，到映出其来源的记录，再到回转自身的头脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a windless lake holding the whole line of hills.
core.cn: 核心意象：无风的湖面托着整排山影。

branches.en: hills upside down in water
branches.cn: 水中倒立的山

branches.en: a report that sounds like the village
branches.cn: 写着全村心声的报告

branches.en: a window seat and a long pause
branches.cn: 窗边的座位与长久的停顿

branches.en: an image that tells the truth of its source
branches.cn: 映出源头的影像

branches.en: a fact seen and then weighed
branches.cn: 看见事实之后加以权衡

intro.en: A Latin verb of bending takes a prefix of return, and the compound passes from rays of light to the movement of thought.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「弯曲」动词接上表返回的前缀，这个复合词便从光线走到了思想的运动。

latinIntro.en: The base is flectere, to bend, with re- meaning back; the participle reflexus feeds the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 flectere（弯曲），re- 表「往回」；分词 reflexus 供给名词形式。

definition_en: a machine or cabinet that keeps food cold; a large cooling apparatus for storage
core_image: 厨房角落里嗡嗡作响的白色机器，门上贴满便签
scene: 厨房角落那台白色的机器整夜嗡嗡作响，门上贴着孩子的画和几张便签。She kept the milk in the refrigerator overnight.
sceneCN: 这里 refrigerator 是「冰箱」（第 1 个义项：家用冷藏电器）；句意为她把牛奶放在冰箱里过夜。画面里可留意：白色机器、门上的画与便签、夜里的嗡鸣。

senses.title: A kitchen appliance
senses.definition: a household cabinet, usually electric, that keeps food cold
senses.definitionCN: 通常用电的、使食物保持低温的家用箱柜
senses.example: She kept the milk in the refrigerator overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 她把牛奶放在冰箱里过夜。
senses.why: The Latin name is simply a thing that makes cold, and the kitchen cabinet is the most familiar such thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名称的意思就是「使冷的东西」，而厨房里的箱柜是最为人熟悉的那一个。

senses.title: A large cooling unit
senses.definition: a large machine or room used to keep goods cold in shops or industry
senses.definitionCN: 商店或工业中用来使货物保持低温的大型机器或房间
senses.example: The fish was stored in a walk-in refrigerator behind the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼存放在店后的大型冷藏库里。
senses.why: The same word serves the home and the trade: both are boxes where cold is made and held.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词家用与商用都管：两者都是制造并保持低温的箱子。

intro.en: Refrigerator is a modern Latin name built from the verb to cool: it means the thing that makes cold.
intro.cn: refrigerator 是用「使冷」的动词构成的近代拉丁名称，意思就是「使冷的东西」。

items.en: Frigus meant cold, and it is the source of the whole family.
items.cn: frigus 意为寒冷，是整个词族的来源。

items.en: Frigerare meant to cool something, built on frigus.
items.cn: frigerare 意为使某物变冷，由 frigus 构成。

items.en: Refrigerare added re- and meant to cool down or refresh, often of fevered patients.
items.cn: refrigerare 加上 re-，意为使冷却或使清爽，常用于发热的病人。

items.en: Writers of the nineteenth century formed refrigerator from the verb and the ending -ator, one that does.
items.cn: 十九世纪的写作者用该动词加词尾 -ator（做某事者）造出 refrigerator。

items.en: English applied the name to the ice box, and later to the electric cabinet in every kitchen.
items.cn: 英语先用它指冰柜，后来又指每间厨房里的电动箱柜。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same cooling family; the near-meaning group gathers names for cold storage.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「制冷」词族的词；近义组收表冷藏器具的名称。

entries.definition: A compartment or machine for freezing food.
A container that keeps things cool.
An old-fashioned box cooled with ice.

normalIntro.en: The word is literally a cold-maker: a box that produces and holds cold so that food lasts.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词字面上就是「造冷者」：一个制造并保持低温、让食物放得更久的箱子。

normal.en: Frigus is cold, and the machine is the thing that makes cold.
normal.cn: frigus 是寒冷，而这台机器就是造冷的东西。

normal.en: Refrigerate the milk, and the refrigerator keeps it cold.
normal.cn: 把牛奶冷藏，冰箱就让它保持低温。

normal.en: The ending ator marks the doer, as in elevator and generator.
normal.cn: 词尾 ator 标记「做某事者」，如 elevator 与 generator。

normal.en: A walk-in refrigerator is big enough to walk inside.
normal.cn: walk-in refrigerator 大到可以走进去。

normal.en: Refrigeration is the process; the refrigerator is the box.
normal.cn: refrigeration 是过程，refrigerator 是箱子。

abstract.en: Cold is not created but moved, and the machine only moves it faster.
abstract.cn: 冷并非被造出，只是被搬运，而机器只是搬得更快。

abstract.en: A refrigerator is a promise that tomorrow will taste like today.
abstract.cn: 冰箱是一个承诺：明天的味道会像今天一样。

abstract.en: The same Latin verb once cooled a fever and now cools a bottle.
abstract.cn: 同一个拉丁动词曾给发热者降温，如今给瓶子降温。

examples.en: She kept the milk in the refrigerator overnight.
examples.cn: 她把牛奶放在冰箱里过夜。

examples.en: The fish was stored in a walk-in refrigerator behind the shop.
examples.cn: 鱼存放在店后的大型冷藏库里。

examples.en: Open the refrigerator door and let the cold air out slowly.
examples.cn: 打开冰箱门，让冷气慢慢散出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（加强）加 friger（冷）加 ator（做某事者）：专门造冷的东西，就是冰箱。

root: 拉丁 frigus（寒冷）→ frigerare（使冷）→ refrigerare（使冷却）→ 近代拉丁 refrigerator（造冷者）→ 英语 refrigerator；同族有 refrigerate、refrigeration、refrigerant。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a cold-maker; the senses move from the household cabinet to the large cooling room of a shop.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「造冷之物」；义项从家用箱柜，到商店里的大型冷藏库。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white machine humming all night in a kitchen corner, covered with notes.
core.cn: 核心意象：厨房角落里嗡嗡作响、贴满便签的白色机器。

branches.en: milk on a kitchen shelf
branches.cn: 厨房层架上的牛奶

branches.en: a cold room behind a fish shop
branches.cn: 鱼店后面的冷藏室

branches.en: the same cold in a home and a trade
branches.cn: 家中与店里的同一种冷

branches.en: a child's drawing taped to the door
branches.cn: 贴在门上的孩子的画

branches.en: a heavy door that seals a room
branches.cn: 封住房间的厚门

intro.en: A Latin word for cold becomes a verb of cooling, and the agent ending then names the machine that does it.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表「寒冷」的词先变成「使冷」的动词，施动者词尾随后命名做这件事的机器。

latinIntro.en: The base is frigus, cold, with frigerare to cool, re- again, and -ator one who does.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 frigus（寒冷），frigerare 意为使冷，re- 表「再次」，-ator 指做某事者。

definition_zh: 拒绝；不肯接受；（名词）垃圾；废弃物
definition_en: to say that you will not do or accept something; (noun) unwanted material that is thrown away
core_image: 背转身去伸出的手：东西递过来，他收回双手扭开头
scene: 门口推销员把传单递过来，男孩摇摇头背过身。The boy refused to take the flyer at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 refused 是「拒绝、不肯」（第 1 个义项：拒绝做某事）；句意为男孩在门口拒绝接过传单。画面里可留意：伸出的手、摇头的动作、转过去的背。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「拒绝；回绝」
动词加施动者后缀，义为「拒绝者」（较少用）

senses.title: To say no to an action or request
senses.definition: to say firmly that you will not do something that someone asks or wants
senses.definitionCN: 明确表示不肯做别人要求或希望的事
senses.example: She refused to answer any questions without a lawyer.
senses.exampleCN: 没有律师在场，她拒绝回答任何问题。
senses.why: The Latin root means to pour back; refusing is figuratively 'pouring back' the request, returning it unaccepted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根义为「倒回去」；拒绝好比把递来的请求原样「倒回去」，不接受、不承接，于是成为本义。

senses.title: To not accept something offered
senses.definition: to not accept something that is offered or given to you
senses.definitionCN: 不接受别人提供或给予的东西
senses.example: He refused the money because it felt like a bribe.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒收那笔钱，因为那像是贿赂。
senses.why: The same pouring-back image applies to objects: what is offered flows back to the giver.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「倒回去」的画面也适用于实物：递来的东西又被「倒」回给递出者，形成拒收义。

senses.title: To not give something that is wanted
senses.definition: to not allow someone to have something they ask for
senses.definitionCN: 不答应给别人想要的东西
senses.example: The officials refused them entry without tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 没有票，工作人员不让他们入场。
senses.why: Refusing can point the other direction: instead of pushing back what comes to you, you hold back what others ask from you.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝也可以反向发生：不是把收到的推回去，而是把别人来要的东西扣住不给，于是产生「不予」义。

senses.title: Unwanted material thrown away (noun)
senses.definition: material that is no longer wanted and is thrown away, read as /ˈrefjuːs/
senses.definitionCN: 不再需要而被丢弃的材料，重音前移读作 /ˈrefjuːs/
senses.example: Plastic refuse was piled along the river bank.
senses.exampleCN: 塑料垃圾堆在河岸边。
senses.why: What has been 'poured back' by everyone is finally rejected as worthless; the rejected stream becomes refuse.
senses.whyCN: 被所有人「倒回去」、拒收的东西最终成了无用之物；这条被拒的「流」沉淀为名词 refuse，即垃圾。

intro.en: Refuse flows from Latin refluxere through Old French, keeping the image of something poured back.
intro.cn: refuse 经由拉丁语与古法语一路流变，核心意象始终是「倒回去的东西」。

items.en: refluxare / refundere family: re- (back) + fundere (to pour), 'to pour back'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ fundere（倒、流），义为「倒回去」。

items.en: Old French refuser meant 'to reject, refuse'.
items.cn: 古法语 refuser 意为「拒绝；否决」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the 14th century meaning to decline or reject.
items.cn: 动词在十四世纪进入英语，表示拒绝、不接受。

items.en: The noun sense of rejected, worthless material developed in Middle English from the same image.
items.cn: 「被拒之物」的名词义也出自同一意象，在中古英语期形成。

items.en: The stress split settled: refuse (verb) on the second syllable, refuse (waste) on the first.
items.cn: 现代英语中重音分化：动词 refuse 重音在后，名词 refuse（垃圾）重音在前。

note.en: These neighbours of refuse differ in strength or direction of the refusal.
note.cn: 下列词与 refuse 在拒绝的强度或方向上有所差别。

entries.definitionCN: 拒绝；回绝（refuse 的名词形式）
庇护；避难（拼写与名词 refuse 极近，词义毫无关联）

entries.definition: a person forced to flee their home
entries.definitionCN: 难民（与 refuse 拼写相近但不同源义）

entries.definition: to throw back as not good enough
entries.definitionCN: 否决；摒弃（更强调判为不合格）

entries.definition: to refuse to admit or give
entries.definitionCN: 否认；拒绝给予（对象多为说法或权利）

normalIntro.en: Root-based reminders for refuse.
normalIntro.cn: refuse 的词根式记忆提示。

normal.en: re- (back) + fus (pour): pour the offer back to the giver.
normal.cn: re-（回）+ fus（流）：把递来的东西「倒」回去，即拒绝。

normal.en: Same root family as fluent, fluid, influence — all about flowing.
normal.cn: 与 fluent、fluid、influence 同属「流动」词族。

normal.en: Verb stress: reFUSE; noun stress: REFuse (waste).
normal.cn: 动词重音在后 reFUSE；名词（垃圾）重音在前 REFuse。

normal.en: refusal is the noun twin: a flat refusal = a firm no.
normal.cn: refusal 是它的名词孪生：a flat refusal 即断然拒绝。

normal.en: Compare reject: re- (back) + ject (throw), a harsher throw-back.
normal.cn: 对照 reject：re-（回）+ ject（扔），是更用力的「扔回去」。

abstract.en: Picture water poured from your cup straight back into the pot.
abstract.cn: 想象杯中的水被原样倒回壶里——拒绝就是倒回去。

abstract.en: See a closed door with hands folded: the request never enters.
abstract.cn: 看见一扇关着的门与合起的双手：请求进不来。

abstract.en: Imagine a heap of returned parcels beside the river: that is refuse.
abstract.cn: 想象河边一堆被退回的包裹：那便是垃圾 refuse。

examples.en: She refused to sign the contract without reading it first.
examples.cn: 没有先读完合同，她拒绝签字。

examples.en: The city sends two trucks for refuse collection every morning.
examples.cn: 这座城市每天早上派两辆卡车清运垃圾。

examples.en: He politely declined the invitation, but flatly refused the bribe.
examples.cn: 他客气地谢绝了邀请，却断然拒绝了贿赂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞福斯」——「瑞」雪送来的「福」也被「撕」掉退回去：把好事退回去就是拒绝；联想 refused＝退回去了。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ fundere（倒、流），「倒回去」→ 拒绝；被众人倒回去之物 → 垃圾。名词动词重音分化：动词 /rɪˈfjuːz/，名词 /ˈrefjuːs/。

sensesIntro.en: From pouring back a request, to pushing back an offer, to holding back a gift, to the pile of what nobody accepts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从倒回去请求，到退回实物，到扣住不给，再到无人接收的废弃物，一条「回流」主线贯穿四义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pouring back what comes
core.cn: 核心意象：把递来的东西倒回去

branches.en: Saying no to a requested action.
branches.cn: 对被要求的事说不（义项 01）。

branches.en: An offered object flows back to the giver.
branches.cn: 递来的实物被退回（义项 02）。

branches.en: Holding back what others ask for.
branches.cn: 别人来要的东西不予（义项 03）。

branches.en: What is refused and worthless accumulates as waste.
branches.cn: 被拒且无用之物堆积成垃圾（义项 03、04）。

branches.en: Denial of action and rejection of object share one image.
branches.cn: 拒绝做事与拒收实物同出一源（义项 01、02）。

intro.en: Refuse carries the Latin pour-structure re- + fus.
intro.cn: refuse 携带拉丁语「倒流」结构 re- + fus。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives from fundere (to pour).
latinIntro.cn: 来自 fundere（倒、流）的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: to pour together and mix up

definition_en: to consider someone or something in a particular way; respect or esteem; to look at steadily
core_image: 老师把一份作业翻看两遍，然后缓缓点头
scene: 老师把那份作业翻来覆去看了两遍，最后缓缓点了点头。The teacher regarded the essay as the best in the class.
sceneCN: 这里 regarded 是 regard 的过去式，取「看待」（第 1 个义项：以某种眼光认为）；句意为老师认为这篇作文是全班最好的。画面里可留意：翻看两遍的动作、缓缓点头。

senses.title: To consider in a way
senses.definition: to think of someone or something in a particular manner
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式认为某人或某物
senses.example: The teacher regarded the essay as the best in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师认为这篇作文是全班最好的。
senses.why: The word begins with a steady look: to regard a thing is first to fix the eyes on it, and then to fix a judgment on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始于凝神一看：先让目光落在某物上，再让判断落在它上面。

senses.title: Respect or esteem
senses.definition: a feeling of admiration and careful attention toward someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的钦佩与郑重对待
senses.example: The old craftsman is held in high regard by everyone in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上人人都十分敬重这位老匠人。
senses.why: When the steady look carries weight, it becomes esteem: the one who is looked at long is the one who is valued.
senses.whyCN: 当这种凝神注视带上分量，它就变成敬重：被看得最久的人，也是被看重的人。

senses.title: To look at steadily
senses.definition: to look at someone or something with attention, often without speaking
senses.definitionCN: 带着注意看某人或某物，常常不出声
senses.example: She regarded the stranger for a long moment before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她注视了那陌生人好一会儿才答话。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense, and it keeps the original image of eyes held on a face.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的一义，它保留了「目光停在一个人脸上」的原始意象。

intro.en: Regard is a French word of watching: a Germanic verb of guarding took a French prefix, and English received it as a steady look.
intro.cn: regard 是一个来自法语的「看」的词：日耳曼语的「看守」动词接上法语前缀，英语接收它时意为凝神注视。

items.en: A Germanic verb of watching and guarding lies behind the French word for looking.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表「看守、注视」的动词，是法语「看」这个词的后盾。

items.en: Old French garder meant to guard or keep, and English kept it as guard.
items.cn: 古法语 garder 意为看守、保留，英语把它保留为 guard。

items.en: Regarder added the intensive prefix re- and meant to look at closely.
items.cn: regarder 加上加强语气的前缀 re-，意为仔细地看。

items.en: English took regard as both a look and a care, and the verb followed the noun.
items.cn: 英语把 regard 同时用作「注视」与「关切」，动词义随后跟上。

items.en: High regard and kind regards grew from the same root: attention paid becomes respect, and respect becomes a greeting.
items.cn: high regard 与 kind regards 出自同一词根：投去的注意变成敬重，敬重又变成问候。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the French verb of guarding; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of judging and looking.
note.cn: 形近组收由法语「看守」动词构成的词；近义组收表示评判与观看的动词。

entries.definition: To think of in a certain way.
To regard in a particular way.

normalIntro.en: The word is a long look: first the eyes rest on a thing, then the mind decides what it is worth.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一次长久的注视：先让目光停在某物上，再让心思判定它值多少。

normal.en: Regard as means to hold an opinion about something.
normal.cn: regard as 指对某物持某种看法。

normal.en: To regard a person is to look, and to regard them highly is to look up.
normal.cn: regard 一个人是看，regard 得高就是敬重。

normal.en: In this regard is a formal way of saying in this matter.
normal.cn: in this regard 是「在这方面」的正式说法。

normal.en: Give my regards means pass on my greetings.
normal.cn: give my regards 指代我问候。

normal.en: Regardless drops the regard, and carries on without looking.
normal.cn: regardless 丢掉了「看」，不瞧一眼就继续。

abstract.en: How we regard a person decides how we treat them.
abstract.cn: 我们如何看待一个人，决定了我们如何对待他。

abstract.en: To be held in high regard is to be looked at with care.
abstract.cn: 被十分敬重，就是被郑重地看待。

abstract.en: A regard that never becomes action is only a look.
abstract.cn: 从不化为行动的尊重，只是一眼注视。

examples.en: The teacher regarded the essay as the best in the class.
examples.cn: 老师认为这篇作文是全班最好的。

examples.en: The old craftsman is held in high regard by everyone in the town.
examples.cn: 镇上人人都十分敬重这位老匠人。

examples.en: She regarded the stranger for a long moment before answering.
examples.cn: 她注视了那陌生人好一会儿才答话。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（一再）加 gard（看守、看）：一再地看一个人，就是在打量他、评价他、敬重他。

root: 日耳曼语 wardon（看守）→ 古法语 garder（看守）→ regarder（仔细看）→ 英语 regard；re- 在此是加强语气的前缀，词根并非拉丁语，因此拉丁条目只列前缀以外的法语与英语形式。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a steady look; the senses move from forming a view, to holding someone in esteem, to watching silently.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「凝神的注视」；义项从形成看法，到把人放在敬重的位置，再到默默观看。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teacher reading an essay twice and then nodding slowly.
core.cn: 核心意象：老师把一份作业翻看两遍，缓缓点头。

branches.en: an essay called the best
branches.cn: 被评为最好的一篇作文

branches.en: an old craftsman respected by a town
branches.cn: 被全镇敬重的老匠人

branches.en: a stranger watched before an answer
branches.cn: 答话前被注视的陌生人

branches.en: a look that turns into a standing
branches.cn: 注视升为声望

branches.en: watching first, judging after
branches.cn: 先看，后判断

intro.en: A Germanic verb of guarding took a French prefix of intensity, and the compound passed into English as a steady, weighing look.
intro.cn: 日耳曼语表「看守」的动词接上法语中表加强的前缀，这个复合词进入英语，意为凝神而带分量的注视。

latinIntro.en: The stem is the French garder of Germanic origin; re- here intensifies rather than repeats, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是源自日耳曼语的法语 garder；这里的 re- 表加强而非重复，因此不列拉丁词根。

definition_en: to feel sorry about something one has done or failed to do; a feeling of sorrow over what cannot be changed; a polite refusal
core_image: 一封没有寄出的信被反复拿起又放回抽屉
scene: 抽屉里有一封始终没有寄出的信，他反复拿起来，又放回去。He regretted the words as soon as they left his mouth.
sceneCN: 这里 regretted 是 regret 的过去式，取「后悔」（第 1 个义项：为自己做过的事感到懊悔）；句意为话一出口他就后悔了。画面里可留意：被反复拿起又放回的信。

senses.title: To feel sorry for one's act
senses.definition: to wish one had not done something one did
senses.definitionCN: 希望自己没有做过某件已做的事
senses.example: He regretted the words as soon as they left his mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 话一出口他就后悔了。
senses.why: The word is a looking back with sorrow: the mind turns to a past act and finds it painful to hold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「带着悲伤的回望」：心思转向过去的某个举动，发现它难以承受。

senses.title: Sorrow over what cannot change
senses.definition: to feel sad about a fact or a loss that one cannot alter
senses.definitionCN: 对无法改变的事实或失去感到难过
senses.example: We regret that the museum will close for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆冬季将闭馆，我们对此感到遗憾。
senses.why: When the past act is not one's own, the same sorrow becomes a formal expression of sympathy.
senses.whyCN: 当过去的举动并非自己所做，同样的悲伤就变为一种正式的惋惜。

senses.title: A polite refusal
senses.definition: a polite message declining an invitation, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 婉言谢绝邀请，常用复数
senses.example: She sent her regrets and stayed home with the children.
senses.exampleCN: 她致意婉辞，留在家中陪孩子。
senses.why: To decline politely is to wrap a no in sorrow, and the plural regrets becomes the note that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 礼貌地拒绝，就是用歉意包住一个「不」，而复数的 regrets 就是承载它的那张便条。

intro.en: Regret is a northern French word of lamenting; its first element is not the Latin prefix of repetition but the opening of a verb of weeping.
intro.cn: regret 是法国北部一个表「哀叹」的词；它的第一个成分不是拉丁表重复的前缀，而是一个「哭泣」动词的开头。

items.en: Old French regreter meant to bewail or lament, and it is the immediate source of the English word.
items.cn: 古法语 regreter 意为哀叹或悲悼，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: The second element probably comes from a Germanic verb of weeping or greeting with tears.
items.cn: 第二个成分很可能出自一个日耳曼语中表哭泣的动词。

items.en: The re- here strengthens the lament rather than repeating it, so the word means to weep over, not to weep again.
items.cn: 这里的 re- 加强「哀叹」的语气而非重复动作，所以这个词意为「为……悲叹」，不是「再哭一次」。

items.en: English borrowed regret in the sense of sorrow for something past or beyond remedy.
items.cn: 英语借入 regret 时，其义为对已过去或无可挽回之事的悲伤。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the plural regrets had become a polite formula for declining an invitation.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，复数形式 regrets 已成为婉拒邀请的客套说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for sorrow over the past.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一词干构成的词；近义组收表示对过去之事感到悲伤的词。

entries.definition: Deep guilt for a wrong done.
Sorrow that turns one from sin.
A statement of sorrow for a fault.

normalIntro.en: The word is a backward look that hurts: it names the pain of a past act and the polite sorrow of a refusal.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一次令人疼痛的回望：它命名对过去举动的痛感，也命名婉拒时客气的歉意。

normal.en: Regret doing something means you wish you had not done it.
normal.cn: regret doing something 指希望自己没做过。

normal.en: Regret to inform is the heavy opening of bad news.
normal.cn: regret to inform 是坏消息沉重的开头。

normal.en: Have no regrets means you would do it all again.
normal.cn: have no regrets 指你愿意再来一遍。

normal.en: The past tense doubles the t: regretted and regretting.
normal.cn: 过去式双写 t：regretted 与 regretting。

normal.en: Send one's regrets is to decline politely, not to grieve.
normal.cn: send one's regrets 是礼貌谢绝，不是哀悼。

abstract.en: Regret is memory with a verdict attached.
abstract.cn: 后悔是附带了判决的记忆。

abstract.en: A life without regret may be a life without attention.
abstract.cn: 毫无悔意的人生，也许是毫不用心的人生。

abstract.en: The polite regret is society's way of softening a no.
abstract.cn: 客气的遗憾，是社会把「不」说得柔软的方式。

examples.en: He regretted the words as soon as they left his mouth.
examples.cn: 话一出口他就后悔了。

examples.en: We regret that the museum will close for the winter.
examples.cn: 博物馆冬季将闭馆，我们对此感到遗憾。

examples.en: She sent her regrets and stayed home with the children.
examples.cn: 她致意婉辞，留在家中陪孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（一再）加 gret（哀叹）：一再为过去的事叹息，就是后悔；对无法改变的事叹息，就是遗憾。

root: 古法语 regreter（哀叹、悲悼，第二个成分可能出自日耳曼语表哭泣的动词）→ 英语 regret；re- 在此是加强语气，不是「再次」前缀。同族有 regretful、regrettable、regrettably。

sensesIntro.en: The core is sorrow turned backward; the senses move from regret for one's own act, to sorrow over what cannot change, to a polite refusal.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「转向过去的悲伤」；义项从为自己的举动后悔，到为无法改变之事遗憾，再到礼貌的婉拒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unsent letter taken out of a drawer and put back again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封没有寄出的信被反复拿起又放回抽屉。

branches.en: words that cannot be recalled
branches.cn: 收不回来的话

branches.en: a museum closing for winter
branches.cn: 冬季闭馆的博物馆

branches.en: a note declining an invitation
branches.cn: 一封谢绝邀请的便条

branches.en: a deed of one's own and a fact of the world
branches.cn: 自己的作为与世间的事实

branches.en: sorrow felt and sorrow sent as a message
branches.cn: 心里的遗憾与寄出的遗憾

intro.en: A French verb of lamenting enters English whole, and its intensifying prefix is often mistaken for the Latin prefix of repetition.
intro.cn: 一个法语表哀叹的动词整词进入英语，其加强语气的前缀常被误认作拉丁表重复的前缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here: the word is French, with a Germanic element, so only the French and English forms are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根：这个词来自法语，含日耳曼语成分，因此只列法语与英语形式。

definition_en: a connection between two or more things; a member of one's family; the way people or countries deal with each other
core_image: 家谱图上两条分支在同一个名字处交汇
scene: 摊开的家谱图上，两条支线在同一个名字处交汇。There is no relation between the two numbers.
sceneCN: 这里 relation 是「关联」（第 1 个义项：事物之间的联系）；句意为这两个数字之间没有关联。画面里可留意：家谱图上交汇的两条支线。

senses.title: A connection between things
senses.definition: the way two or more things are connected or affect each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个事物相互连接或影响的方式
senses.example: There is no relation between the two numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个数字之间没有关联。
senses.why: The noun names what is produced when one thing is carried back to another: a line drawn between them.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名「把一物带回另一物」时产生的东西：两者之间画出的一条线。

senses.title: A family member
senses.definition: a person connected to another by blood or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻而与另一人相连的人
senses.example: She is a distant relation of the old painter.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那位老画家的远亲。
senses.why: Kinship is the oldest form of connection, so the word for a link also names the people joined by it.
senses.whyCN: 血缘是最古老的连接形式，因此表「联系」的词也用来指被这条线连起来的人。

senses.title: Official dealings
senses.definition: the way groups or countries deal with one another, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 团体或国家之间往来的方式，通常用复数
senses.example: The two countries restored diplomatic relations after ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 两国在十年之后恢复了外交关系。
senses.why: States also stand in relation to each other, and the plural names the whole web of those dealings.
senses.whyCN: 国家之间也彼此处于关系之中，复数形式便命名这整张往来之网。

intro.en: Relation is the noun of relate, and like refer it comes from the Latin verb of carrying back.
intro.cn: relation 是 relate 的名词，与 refer 一样出自拉丁语表「带回」的动词。

items.en: Referre meant to carry back and to report, built on ferre, to carry.
items.cn: referre 意为带回与报告，由 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: Relatio named a bringing back, and Latin writers used it for a report to a body and for a logical connection.
items.cn: relatio 指一种带回，拉丁作家用它表示向机构作报告，也表示逻辑上的关联。

items.en: Old French relacion carried the sense of a report and of a connection between things.
items.cn: 古法语 relacion 兼具「报告」与「事物之间关联」两义。

items.en: English extended the noun to people connected by blood, since kinship is a relation in the plainest sense.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词扩展到有血缘的人，因为亲属是最直白的一种关系。

items.en: In the plural, relations came to name the official dealings between states and groups.
items.cn: 在复数形式中，relations 用来指国家与团体之间的正式往来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns of the same carrying family; the near-meaning group gathers words for connection and kinship.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词族的名词；近义组收表示联系与亲属的词。

normalIntro.en: The noun names the line drawn between two things, the people joined by blood, and the dealings between states.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词指两物之间画出的那条线、被血缘连起来的人，以及国家之间的往来。

normal.en: Relate is the act, relation is the line it draws.
normal.cn: relate 是动作，relation 是它画出的线。

normal.en: In relation to means with regard to.
normal.cn: in relation to 意为关于、相对于。

normal.en: A close relation is a near relative, not a near idea.
normal.cn: a close relation 指近亲，不是相近的想法。

normal.en: Diplomatic relations are kept in the plural.
normal.cn: diplomatic relations 用复数。

normal.en: Public relations is the work of managing how people see you.
normal.cn: public relations 是管理公众看法的行当。

abstract.en: A relation is not a thing but a line between things.
abstract.cn: 关系不是一个东西，而是东西之间的一条线。

abstract.en: Every relation changes both sides a little.
abstract.cn: 每一种关系都会稍稍改变双方。

abstract.en: To bear no relation to something is to share no line with it.
abstract.cn: 与某物毫无关系，就是与它不共用任何一条线。

examples.en: There is no relation between the two numbers.
examples.cn: 这两个数字之间没有关联。

examples.en: She is a distant relation of the old painter.
examples.cn: 她是那位老画家的远亲。

examples.en: The two countries restored diplomatic relations after ten years.
examples.cn: 两国在十年之后恢复了外交关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: relate（联系）加 ion（名词尾）：被联系起来的这条线是关联，被这条线连起来的人是亲属，国与国之间的线是交往。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回、报告）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 拉丁 relatio（带回、关联）→ 古法语 relacion → 英语 relation；同族有 relate、relationship、relative、relational。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line drawn by carrying one thing back to another; the senses move from a link between things, to people joined by blood, to dealings between states.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把一物带回另一物所画出的线」；义项从事物之间的联系，到被血缘连起来的人，再到国家之间的往来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two branches of a family tree meeting at one name.
core.cn: 核心意象：家谱图上两条分支在同一个名字处交汇。

branches.en: two figures with no line between
branches.cn: 之间没有线的两个数字

branches.en: a distant cousin at a funeral
branches.cn: 葬礼上的一位远亲

branches.en: two embassies reopened
branches.cn: 重新开馆的两国使馆

branches.en: a line between numbers and a line between people
branches.cn: 数字之间的线与人与人之间的线

branches.en: family ties and state ties
branches.cn: 家族纽带与国家纽带

intro.en: The noun of carrying back takes the Latin ending of action, and the result names both a logical link and a family tie.
intro.cn: 表「带回」的名词接上拉丁表行为的词尾，结果便同时命名逻辑上的关联与家族中的纽带。

latinIntro.en: The base is relatus, carried back, with -io forming the noun relatio.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 relatus（被带回的），-io 构成名词 relatio。

definition_en: the way two people or groups deal with each other over time; a connection between two things; a romantic partnership
core_image: 两把旧椅子被摆得很近，中间的地面已经磨得发亮
scene: 靠窗摆着两把旧椅子，中间那块地板被来回走动磨得发亮。They built a working relationship over ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 relationship 是「关系」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间长期相处的方式）；句意为他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。画面里可留意：靠得很近的两把椅子、磨亮的地板。

senses.title: A connection between people
senses.definition: the way two people or groups behave toward each other over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或群体在一段时间里彼此相处的方式
senses.example: They built a working relationship over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。
senses.why: The suffix -ship turns a relation into a continuing state, so the word names something kept up over time rather than a single link.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 把 relation 变成一种持续的状态，因此这个词指的是长期维持的东西，而不是一次性的连接。

senses.title: A connection between things
senses.definition: the way two facts, amounts, or ideas are connected
senses.definitionCN: 两个事实、数量或观念相互联系的方式
senses.example: Researchers found a relationship between sleep and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者发现睡眠与记忆之间存在关联。
senses.why: Things, like people, can be set beside each other, and the line between them is also called a relationship.
senses.whyCN: 事物和人一样可以被并置，而它们之间的那条线也叫 relationship。

senses.title: A romantic partnership
senses.definition: a close personal connection in which two people love each other
senses.definitionCN: 两人彼此相爱的一种亲密关系
senses.example: They were in a relationship for three years before they married.
senses.exampleCN: 他们恋爱三年后才结婚。
senses.why: When the personal connection is the closest kind, the general word is used without any further qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 当这种私人联系是最亲密的一种时，这个泛称就不再加任何限定词。

intro.en: Relationship is relation plus the old English suffix of state: a link that is kept going, not a link merely drawn.
intro.cn: relationship 是 relation 加上古英语表状态的后缀：一条被持续维持的线，而不是仅仅画出的线。

items.en: Relatio meant a bringing back and a connection between things.
items.cn: relatio 意为带回，以及事物之间的关联。

items.en: English relation named a connection, a report, and a kinsman.
items.cn: 英语 relation 指关联、报告与亲属。

items.en: The Old English suffix -ship means a state or a condition, as in friendship and hardship.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -ship 意为状态或境况，如 friendship 与 hardship。

items.en: Putting -ship on relation produced a word for a connection that lasts and is maintained.
items.cn: 把 -ship 加在 relation 上，造出了表示持久且被维系的关系的词。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became the ordinary term for a couple's partnership.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词成为指伴侣关系的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same connection family; the near-meaning group gathers words for ties and partnerships.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「联系」词族的词；近义组收表示纽带与伴侣关系的词。

entries.definition: A link between things or people.
A strong feeling that ties people.

normalIntro.en: The word is a relation with a duration: something two sides keep up, day after day.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是有时间长度的 relation：双方一天天维持下去的东西。

normal.en: Relation plus ship: a relation that is kept like a ship at sea.
normal.cn: relation 加 ship：像船在海上一样被维持的 relation。

normal.en: A working relationship is built, not found.
normal.cn: a working relationship 是建起来的，不是捡到的。

normal.en: A relationship between figures is a pattern, not a person.
normal.cn: 数字之间的关系是一种模式，不是人。

normal.en: In a relationship means the couple is committed.
normal.cn: in a relationship 指两人已经在交往。

normal.en: The ship in relationship is a suffix of state, not a boat.
normal.cn: relationship 里的 ship 是表状态的后缀，不是船。

abstract.en: A relationship is a bridge that both ends must repair.
abstract.cn: 关系是一座两端都得修桥的桥。

abstract.en: What is not maintained quietly returns to being two strangers.
abstract.cn: 不维系的东西，会悄悄退回成两个陌生人。

abstract.en: The quality of a life is largely the quality of its relationships.
abstract.cn: 生活的质地，很大程度上是关系的质地。

examples.en: They built a working relationship over ten years.
examples.cn: 他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。

examples.en: Researchers found a relationship between sleep and memory.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠与记忆之间存在关联。

examples.en: They were in a relationship for three years before they married.
examples.cn: 他们恋爱三年后才结婚。

dict_mnemonic.text: relation（关系）加 ship（状态）：不是画一条线，而是长期维持这种状态，就是 relationship。

root: 拉丁 relatio（带回、关联）→ 英语 relation ＋ 古英语后缀 -ship（状态）→ relationship；同族有 relate、relation、relative、related，词干出自拉丁 ferre（携带）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a link that is kept up; the senses move from a personal connection over time, to a pattern between facts, to a couple's partnership.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被持续维持的线」；义项从长期的人际联系，到事实之间的模式，再到伴侣关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two old chairs set close together, the floor between them worn bright.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把旧椅子被摆得很近，中间的地面已经磨得发亮。

branches.en: a decade of working side by side
branches.cn: 十年并肩工作

branches.en: sleep and memory on one chart
branches.cn: 同一张图上的睡眠与记忆

branches.en: three years before a wedding
branches.cn: 婚礼之前的三年

branches.en: a partnership at work and at home
branches.cn: 工作与家庭中的同一种相伴

branches.en: a pattern between facts and a pattern between people
branches.cn: 事实之间的模式与人之间的模式

intro.en: The noun of connection takes the old English suffix of state, and the compound names a link that continues through time.
intro.cn: 表联系的名词接上古英语表状态的后缀，合成词便命名一条延续于时间中的线。

latinIntro.en: The stem is relatio, a bringing back and a connection; -ship is the English suffix of state.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 relatio（带回、关联）；-ship 是英语表状态的后缀。

definition_en: true only when compared with something else; connected with a particular subject; a member of one's family
core_image: 两个人站在不同高度的台阶上比身高
scene: 两个人站在不同高度的台阶上，看起来竟一样高。Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
sceneCN: 这里 relative 是「相对的」（第 1 个义项：只有在比较中才成立）；句意为幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。画面里可留意：不同高度的台阶、看起来一样高的两人。

senses.title: True only by comparison
senses.definition: not absolute, but true when measured against something else
senses.definitionCN: 非绝对的，只有在与其他事物比较时才成立
senses.example: Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
senses.exampleCN: 幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。
senses.why: The Latin participle means carried back, and a value carried back to another value is measured by it rather than in itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁分词意为「被带回的」，一个数值被带回另一个数值那里，就是以它为准来衡量，而不是就自身而言。

senses.title: Connected with a subject
senses.definition: having a connection with a particular matter
senses.definitionCN: 与某个特定事项有关联
senses.example: The report gathers the facts relative to the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告汇集了与那场事故相关的事实。
senses.why: Something carried back to a question is relevant to it, and the same adjective names that connection.
senses.whyCN: 被带回到某个问题那里的东西就与它有关，同一个形容词命名这种关联。

senses.title: A family member
senses.definition: a person connected to another by blood or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻而与另一人相连的人
senses.example: A distant relative left her the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 一位远亲把那座老房子留给了她。
senses.why: Persons related by blood are quite literally carried back to a common ancestor, and the adjective became a noun for them.
senses.whyCN: 有血缘的人确实可以被带回同一个祖先，于是这个形容词就成了指他们的名词。

intro.en: Relative is the adjective of the Latin participle carried back; what is carried back is measured against something else, or joined to a family.
intro.cn: relative 是拉丁分词「被带回的」所对应的形容词；被带回的东西，要么以别物为尺，要么归入一个家族。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, the root of referre and of the whole rel- family.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带，是 referre 与整个 rel- 词族的根。

items.en: Relatus, the participle of referre, meant carried back or having reference to.
items.cn: relatus 是 referre 的分词，意为被带回的或有所指的。

items.en: Relativus meant having relation to something else, the grammatical and philosophical term.
items.cn: relativus 意为与其他事物有关的，是语法与哲学术语。

items.en: English used the adjective for values that hold only in comparison, as opposed to absolute ones.
items.cn: 英语用这个形容词表示只在比较中成立的数值，与「绝对」相对。

items.en: The noun use for a family member grew from the sense of persons referred to one another by blood.
items.cn: 指亲属的名词用法，由「因血缘而彼此相关的人」这一意义发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same carrying stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of comparison and kinship words.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词干的词；近义组收表比较的形容词与亲属词。

entries.definition: Changing in step with something else.

normalIntro.en: The word means carried back to something else: a value to another value, a fact to a question, a person to a family.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词意为「被带回别处」：数值带回另一数值，事实带回一个问题，人带回一个家族。

normal.en: Relative to means measured against.
normal.cn: relative to 意为以……为参照来衡量。

normal.en: Relative humidity compares moisture with the maximum the air can hold.
normal.cn: relative humidity 把湿度与空气能容纳的最大量相比。

normal.en: A close relative is a near member of the family.
normal.cn: a close relative 是家族中的近亲。

normal.en: Relative importance ranks things against each other.
normal.cn: relative importance 是把事物相互比较后的轻重。

normal.en: Relative and absolute are a pair; one needs the other.
normal.cn: relative 与 absolute 是一对，彼此需要。

abstract.en: Almost everything we call large is only relatively large.
abstract.cn: 我们所说的大，几乎都只是相对地大。

abstract.en: To see things as relative is not to see them as unreal.
abstract.cn: 把事物看作相对的，并不等于把它们看作虚幻的。

abstract.en: A family is the first place where a person is a relative.
abstract.cn: 家庭是一个人最初成为「亲属」的地方。

examples.en: Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
examples.cn: 幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。

examples.en: The report gathers the facts relative to the accident.
examples.cn: 这份报告汇集了与那场事故相关的事实。

examples.en: A distant relative left her the old house.
examples.cn: 一位远亲把那座老房子留给了她。

dict_mnemonic.text: relate（带回、关联）加 ive：必须带回别物才有意义，是相对；与某个问题带回一处，是相关；因血缘被带回一家，是亲戚。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 拉丁 relativus（有关的）→ 英语 relative；同族有 relatively、relativity、relation、relate。
